summary: SAROS is a territorial monitoring platform that helps understand how changes in the Earth's surface can relate to risks and impacts on communities and their livelihoods. Through an interactive interface featuring a 3D globe and geographic views, the project explores radar observations from the NASA-ISRO NISAR mission alongside territorial and socioeconomic information. The platform aims to facilitate the identification of areas requiring attention, show which sectors might be exposed, and communicate preventive measures in accessible language. SAROS is important because it transforms complex geospatial information into useful context to support local conversations and decisions. Its analyses and forecasts are presented with caution: they are tools for exploration and support, not official alerts or guarantees that an event will occur.
details:
SAROS brings together planetary exploration, area-of-interest queries, and the review of terrain changes and potential territorial impacts into a single visual experience. The frontend displays locations on a 3D globe and allows users to explore maps, indicators, historical background, exposed sectors, and recommendations. Its architecture is designed to connect these components with backend services to receive NISAR scenes and measurements, territorial assessments, and socioeconomic data. When processed information is unavailable, the interface can display clearly labeled demonstration data.

The project aims to help authorities, response teams, and communities connect geospatial observations with factors such as housing, agriculture, and infrastructure. In doing so, it makes it easier to prioritize areas for review and communicate why an observed change may warrant attention, without attributing causality or presenting an estimate as a certainty.

The team built SAROS using Next.js, React, TypeScript, and CSS, leveraging Three.js via React Three Fiber for 3D visualization, MapLibre for mapping, and Framer Motion for animations. The backend includes a Flask API, PostgreSQL, and NISAR data processing tools. Its creative approach lies in combining scientific visualization, socioeconomic context, and preventive communication into one interactive experience. The team also accounts for data provenance and quality, analytical uncertainty, accessibility, mobile usability, and the need to clearly distinguish between real and simulated data.
